name: RN1
archetype: In-play two-sided market maker (soccer, tennis, CS2, US sports)
headline: Runs a large in-play market-making book: resting bids on both sides of live soccer, tennis, CS2 and US football markets, about $65M of fills a month. It is off the book when game events hit, before the public price moves. A maker using public data, without that speed, loses money in the same markets, including the families where RN1 earns most.
mechanism: 92% of sampled fills are maker fills on-chain. Complete pairs bought at a median combined 0.982 lock $963,976 in 30 days; the unmatched residual loses $319,040 to adverse selection. Soccer is about 45% of its volume (tennis and esports 40%). Its best families are college football, the WTA, the Champions League, CS2, La Liga and the ATP; NFL and the 'other' soccer leagues lose. Around ESPN scoring plays 1.4% of its passive fills land in the first 5 s (all makers: 4.9%), and makers' fills there lose 26%; after soccer goals it is 6% of touch fills against 13% for other makers, already before the first public price jump (ESPN's timestamp trails that jump by a median 3.5 s).

roc.detail: 79%/month: 30-day PnL $907,319 on peak capital at risk $1,141,785; counting the on-chain collateral too ($2,105,457), at least 28%/month

onchain.detail: 200/200 sampled fills confirmed in Polygon OrderFilled events; 92% maker fills (95% CI 88%-95%), 93% of USDC

match.detail: no public rule predicts which fills are RN1's: reviewer own-tape calm AUC 0.531 (p=0.59), sibling-market jumps 0.563 (p=0.12), ESPN time-since-goal 0.547 (p=0.18). It is significantly absent after ESPN-timed soccer goals (6.0% vs 12.9% of touch fills, p=0.0005, 23 of 32 held-out games), but that describes when it is gone, not when it pulls out

backtest.detail: all families: tape-only two-sided maker on 70 held-out markets -7.8% to -18.9% at 0-30 s (strict), -5.1% to -8.7% at 0-5 s with first-in-queue fills; the wallet's own passive fills there +6.5% (p=0.30); only its profitable families (WTA, ATP, CS2, UCL, La Liga, Serie A, CFB): tape-only two-sided maker on 79 held-out markets -8.3% to -12.8% at 0-30 s (strict), -8.3% to -10.9% at 0-5 s with first-in-queue fills; the wallet's own passive fills there -0.9% (p=0.57); reviewer pause-after-goal maker -2.9% to -5.3% strict, about 0% at-touch (p 0.45-0.82)

replicable.detail: nearly all its volume is in markets with a 1 s delay on incoming taker orders; RN1 cancels inside that delay, before the public price moves, while other makers' fills right after plays lose heavily: copying it needs a sub-second race or a private data feed

persistence.detail: last 30 days p=0.0025; decline vs earlier p=0.41; last 15 vs prior 15 p=0.62; trend p=1.00

reasons: A public-data maker loses money in the same markets at every delay tested, including in RN1's most profitable families.
Its edge is being off the book before the public price moves, which needs faster-than-public game data.
No public rule reproduces which fills it gets.
corrections: Soccer, not tennis/esports, is its largest family (about 45% of volume), and ESPN publishes soccer event times; the reviewer's soccer test is now part of the record.
ROC 79% counts only open positions; with its $1.5-2.4M of on-chain collateral it is still about 28% a month.
The at-touch bound promised by the methodology is now computed for the tape-only maker.
